policy: Use Catholic context only when the product title, category, description, attributes, or verified imagery supports it.

Religious merchandise must not be described as blessed, consecrated, miraculous, protective, grace-giving, Church-approved, or liturgical unless the source explicitly and verifiably establishes that fact.
A devotional article is not automatically a sacramental. A blessing is a separate ecclesial act and must never be inferred from the object itself.
Do not force Catholic keywords onto a generic accessory. Return catholic_relevance as none when evidence is absent or ambiguous.
Distinguish a cross from a crucifix: use crucifix only when the corpus of Christ is explicitly present or verified.

safe_context: The Rosary is a Catholic prayer centered on contemplation of events in the lives of Jesus Christ and the Virgin Mary.
The traditional Rosary mysteries are grouped as Joyful, Luminous, Sorrowful, and Glorious.
Describe bead count, centerpiece, crucifix, material, and construction only when those details are present in the product facts.
The Catholic Catechism lists the Rosary and medals among forms of popular piety surrounding sacramental life.
Popular devotions extend but do not replace the Church's liturgical life.
Do not call an unblessed retail object a sacramental or imply spiritual effects.
Marian refers to the Virgin Mary in Christian and Catholic context.
Our Lady is an English Catholic title for the Virgin Mary.
If the source uses an unclear phrase such as Our Lady of Jesus, do not invent a specific Marian title; prefer a precise generic term such as Marian pendant when supported.
Cross and crucifix are not interchangeable product terms.
A crucifix depicts Christ on the cross; a plain cross does not.
Use the more specific term only when the product facts or verified image support it.
Catholic sacramentals are sacred signs instituted by the Church and include blessings.
Sacramentals do not confer grace in the same way as the sacraments.
Never infer that a product has been blessed, consecrated, or reserved for liturgical use.
First Communion refers to a person's first reception of Holy Communion.
Describe a product as a First Communion gift or accessory only when that use is explicit in the source facts.
